text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Gulf nationals smuggle banned goods to Iraq, Western diplomatic sources say. A U.S. report says the goods are used by Baghdad in developing biological and chemical weapons, they said. Iraq is under a U.N.-imposed trade embargo since its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah to stay one more month in London for recuperation, Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said.
- Communications, Electricity and Water Minister Jassem al-Oun says ministry to establish central station to monitor the Internet.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan left for the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday to attend the Gulf Investment Corp's general assembly and board meetings to be held on Thursday.
- Islamist parliamentarian Mufarej Nahar escapes attempt on life on Tuesday. Nahar accuses an opponent who ran for a parliament seat in the same constituency in the October 1996 elections.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah patronised graduation ceremony at Kuwait University on Tuesday.
- Commerce and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf says a free trade zone with Egypt would boost trade in the region. Kuwait and Egypt are mulling a joint free trade zone.
- Parliament's legal committee approves a bill on forming the Kuwait Human Rights Authority.
